newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE PRICES IN MIXED PICTURE.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE PRICES IN MIXED PICTURE.

text.p: Bucharest bourse shares traded sideways on Wednesday, with investors once again focusing two first-tier stocks which were heavily traded.
Eight stocks went up, 11 dipped and four closed flat.

Two independent indices -- the VAB and BIG -- rose by 0.7 and 0.3 percent respectively, to 548.1 and 556.3 points. The BIG first-tier index edged up by 0.31 percent to 1,788.89 points from the previous session.
The rise in both indices was led by gains in first-tier Azomures fertiliser maker and pharmaceutical maker Terapia, one trader said.
Azomures and Oltchim chemical plant, which is also listed on the first tier, took more than 80 percent of the day's turnover of 4.0 billion lei.
"Continuing selling pressure drove Oltchim's price down in lively trading," one broker said. "It might slip some more on Thursday." Oltchim close 50 lei weaker at 1,350.
Azomures ended 20 lei firmer at 1,870, while Terapia gained 100 lei to close at 3,300.
Antibiotice, a newcomer to the first tier, was on strong demand. It gained 1,300 lei, to close at 3,500, amid thin supply.
"There might be growing interest in pharmaceuticals, so Antibiotice could post higher quotes," another broker said.
Another new stock on the exchange, second-tier oil drilling company Foraj Sonde Ploiesti, attracted some interest but volumes remained thin. It closed 600 lei up from opening quotes at 3,100 lei.
New entry hotelier Turism Transilvania failed to impress the market and had no trading.
On the second tier, dye maker Policolor and engineer Armatura were the most active, both closing higher on stronger demand.
Syringe maker Sanevit, once a bourse star, was suspended from trading for several hours following local press reports that Romania's Health Ministry had suspended a contract with Sasnevit.
Trading resumed later on Wednesday, when the company released a statement saying it would seek a new deal with the ministry under a tender bid planned for later this year.
Sanevit lost 1,000 lei closing at 7,000 lei.
"With market focus on high-caps, the Sanevit incident was not too impressive," one trader said.
Three second-tier stocks had no trade, while six companies were suspended pending announcements.
Over-the-counter market trading details were unavailable.
